findings.title: findings() silently drops non-bulleted text under an unrecognized heading, letting decide() auto-approve over it
findings.detail: findings(_:) only ever records a line as `unsorted` when it is a list item (`if item != nil { found.unsorted.append(text) }`, line 309). When a reviewer writes a real concern as plain prose (no `-`/`*`/number) under a heading Oby doesn't recognise (e.g. "Security concern:\nTokens are logged in plaintext."), the heading-reset branch (lines 301-307) sets `section = nil`, and the following prose line hits the `guard let section else { ... }` branch with `item == nil`, so it is discarded entirely - never added to `blocking`, `later`, or even `unsorted`. If the same review also happens to use a recognised heading elsewhere (e.g. a `Worth doing later:` list), `sorted` becomes true, so `decide()` no longer falls back to the model's own last line; since `findings.blocking` is empty and `findings.unsorted` is also empty (the real finding was dropped, not counted), `decide()` returns `.approved` even though the reviewer's last line said `VERDICT: CHANGES REQUESTED` and flagged a genuine, unclassified problem. This defeats the stated goal of this very change ("never approve over a finding Oby couldn't place"): the `unsorted` safety net only covers content written as markdown list items, not prose, under a heading the parser doesn't know. `aFollowUpReview...`/`findingsOutsideTheKnownHeadingsKeepTheReviewersVerdict` tests only exercise the bulleted case under an unknown heading, not the prose case, so this gap is untested.
